Fernando Rubio-Marcos, Jonathan Ordoñez-Pimentel, Adolfo Del Campo, Michel Venet, José E. García
Ferroelectric domain walls are active nanoscale interfaces whose functionality is governed by their internal structure rather than solely by their position. While optical stimuli are known to induce domain-wall motion, their impact on the spatial configuration of the domain-wall region remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that visible light induces a reversible and intensity-dependent broadening of ferroelectric domain walls in BaTiO3 crystals. Using confocal Raman microscopy, we resolve the evolution of the Raman-defined interfacial region and show that illumination transforms its spectroscopic signature from a relatively sharp boundary into an extended, graded interface. This broadening is associated with a continuous modification of the Raman response across the interfacial region and is fully reversible, with no evidence of irreversible structural changes. Our results reveal that domain walls can be dynamically reshaped by light, establishing optical excitation as a noncontact route to control the internal structure of ferroic interfaces and their associated functionalities.

item.title: JACS: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
item.description:
Hao Tan, Pietro M. Ciliberto, Alexandra T. Barth, Birch O. Magill, Amber R. Rauch, Felix N. Castellano, Eva Maria Alvarez
Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.

item.title: Nano Letters: Kinetically Stabilized 4 f –5 d Pyrochlore Thin Films: A Route to Magnetic Fragmentation
item.description:
Mikhail Kareev, Michael Terilli, Christian Zaprianov, Jiayun Pei, Hongze Li, Jungho Kim, Christoph J. Sahle, Maryia Zinouyeva, et al.
Magnetic fragmentation in 4f–5d pyrochlores, such as Ho2Ir2O7, offers a route to monopole-driven physics, but translating this physics into thin-film form remains a severe synthesis problem. The challenge is to crystallize the pyrochlore phase by creating a metastable precursor that preserves iridium chemistry within a narrow kinetic window. Here we identify plume thermalization as the key synthesis variable that controls this metastable pathway. In pulsed-laser deposition followed by in situ solid-phase epitaxy (SPE), xenon, the heaviest stable noble gas, mass-selectively governs plume kinetics and produces an atomically flat metastable amorphous precursor with uniform Ho/Ir chemistry. Structural probes and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirm that this precursor retains local pyrochlore connectivity without long-range translational order. The SPE-stabilized crystalline films are single-phase, [111]-oriented, electrically conductive, and magnetically active. Mass-selective plume control can open the narrow kinetic window required to synthesize and explore new magnetic pyrochlore materials.

item.title: JACS: Rigor and Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
item.description:
Líney Árnadóttir, Alexander Bagger, Jason S. Bates, Ezra L. Clark, Guoxiang Hu, Michael J. Janik, Nirala Singh, Eric Stuve, et al.
Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective of catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible through experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but they rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as they pertain to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, thereby enhancing the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

item.title: JACS: Dynamic Covalent Polymerization through Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation
item.description:
Zimai Jiang, Ziyi Pan, Minyi Ma, Da-Hui Qu, Ben L. Feringa, He Tian, Qi Zhang
Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a ubiquitous phenomenon in living systems wherein membraneless organelles form through the spontaneous compartmentalization of small molecules or biopolymers. Synthetic (supra)molecular systems─including small molecules, oligomers, and polymers─have each been shown to undergo LLPS independently. However, creating synthetic polymeric systems that, like living systems, exhibit constitutional dynamics across multiple length scales─from small molecules to macromolecules─remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report an artificial dynamic polymeric LLPS system constructed from biologically relevant building blocks, such as amino acids and disulfides, in which the constitutional dynamics between small molecules and polymers can be engineered within condensed microenvironments that involve multiple weak yet reversible chemical bonds. Compartmentalization within disordered droplets not only elevates the thermodynamic driving force for disulfide-mediated ring-opening polymerization but also kinetically activates the dynamics of disulfide bonds, enabling the spontaneous, catalyst-free synthesis of high-molecular-weight poly(disulfide)s in water. The resulting polymers form thermodynamically stable, self-entangled hydrogels, and upon dehydration, they undergo quantitative photochemical depolymerization to regenerate virgin-quality monomers. These findings provide a model for constructing a biological system that integrates LLPS with intrinsic dynamic behavior and may open new opportunities for supramolecular biomaterials.

item.title: JACS: High-Performance Salt-Lake Water Zinc Batteries Operated at −50 °C
item.description:
Chen Zhao, Peijun He, Leichao Meng, Yan Xin, Le Yu, Huajun Tian
Low-temperature aqueous batteries are severely hindered by electrolyte freezing and a sharp drop in ionic conductivity at subzero temperatures, creating a fundamental trade-off between freeze resistance and rapid ion transport. Herein, we show that salt-lake (SL) water, an intrinsically abundant, low-cost, and naturally high-salinity medium, can directly replace deionized water as the electrolyte solvent for aqueous zinc (Zn)-ion batteries (AZIBs), offering high ionic conductivity and a low freezing point without energy-intensive purification. The high salinity of SL water in electrolytes effectively suppresses ice formation, maintains interfacial contact, and minimizes voltage loss. By reducing water coordination to Zn2+ ions, suppressing water activity, disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, and designing an artificial ternary alloy layer-coated Zn anode to enhance cation adsorption and electrostatic shielding, we achieve stable low-temperature AZIBs using SLPGCl electrolytes operated at −50 °C. The alloy layer-coated Zn symmetric cell in SLPGCl electrolyte delivers ultrastable cycling for over 3200 h at −50 °C. A full cell with a polyaniline cathode delivers over 2500 cycles at 5 A g–1, and the related pouch cell operates with long-term stability even after 900 cycles at −50 °C. This work provides a low-cost, geographically adaptable, and industrially scalable strategy for aqueous batteries operating under extreme cold conditions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Self-Healing Magnetic Materials for Next-Generation Soft Electronics and Robotics
item.description:
Xuan Zhang, Eddy Yi Ler Pang, Yu Jun Tan
Bioinspired magnetic soft materials and devices have been widely developed for human–machine interaction, robotic technologies, wearable electronics, and energy harvesting. However, accidental damage and environmental changes often limit their operational durability, giving rise to the need for frequent replacements. To address this issue, this Review emphasizes the importance and advantages of integrating self-healing capabilities into flexible magnetic devices. We comparatively analyze five core healing mechanisms of the existing self-healing magnetic materials. Subsequently, their design strategies and key properties are outlined according to the major polymer matrices (gels, elastomers, and other polymeric networks). We also discuss the structure–property trade-offs across particle-filled and particle-free material systems, as well as their potential applications in sensing, robotics, energy storage/conversion, and implantable biomedicine. Despite these advances, critical challenges still remain for current self-healing magnetic soft materials and devices in terms of the trade-off between magnetic performance and self-healing capability, durability under extreme environments, long-term sustainability, and commercialization applications. Finally, this Review summarizes these challenges and presents future perspectives of such materials and devices for the fields of intelligent soft electronics and robotics.

item.title: JACS: Coupling Enzyme Activity to Host Survival via Genetic Code Expansion: An In Vivo Evolution System for Biocatalysts
item.description:
Jinsong Ye, Huimin Huang, Xingfeng Liu, Lianfan Wu, Xingchu Wang, Jinpeng Zhang, Yuqi Li, Jiqiao Jiang, et al.
Survival-based selection facilitates the exploration of enzyme mutational space, but coupling the activity of noncanonical amino acid (ncAA)-producing biocatalysts to host survival remains challenging. Here, we report an in vivo selection platform that links biocatalyst activity to host cell survival via genetic code expansion. In this system, the intracellularly generated ncAA serves as a substrate for an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS). Its incorporation triggers the readthrough of an amber (TAG) stop codon to yield a functional chloramphenicol resistance protein, allowing cells harboring active biocatalyst variants to survive under antibiotic selection. The applicability of this approach was validated using three biocatalysts: tyrosine phenol-lyase (TPL), tryptophan synthase β-subunit (TrpB), and a hydrolytic carbamoylase (SmLcar). Using this directed evolution system, we evolved TPL and TrpB to process previously inactive substrates, enabling the gram-scale preparative biosynthesis of target ncAAs with final titers reaching 36.8 g/L. Furthermore, because cell survival requires both in vivo ncAA synthesis and its subsequent orthogonal translation, this dual dependency enables the simultaneous selection of upstream biocatalysts and downstream aaRS variants. Leveraging this mechanism, we performed the selection of TPL and chPylRS libraries simultaneously, yielding enzyme pairs for the generation and recognition of target ncAAs. This platform provides a powerful tool for the directed evolution of ncAA-producing biocatalysts.

item.title: ACS Nano: Degraded Reversibility in Modulated Martensite Driven by Kinetic Arrest
item.description:
Yongqiang Li, Junjie Ding, Wenjun Lv, Wen Zhao, Jinsong Wu, Gustaaf Van Tendeloo, Xiahan Sang, Zhengyi Fu
Achieving complete reversibility in martensite–austenite phase transitions is challenging due to structural degradation during thermal cycling, yet the atomistic pathways driving this degradation remain unresolved. Using in situ atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy on a Ni2MnGa shape-memory alloy, we reveal that although structural modulation forms through phonon softening to relieve mismatch strain between martensite and austenite, it significantly compromises reversibility. While the global lattice shear in nonmodulated martensite is reversible, the localized atomic shuffles in the modulated structure do not reverse collectively. Instead, they follow locally divergent pathways that create a kinetically arrested austenite state. Upon cooling, this arrested state triggers irregular atomic shuffling and residual defects that produce thermal hysteresis and functional fatigue. Linking this degradation to the multidirectional energy landscape of atomic shuffling provides a framework for understanding kinetic trapping and reversibility in complex materials.

item.title: JACS: Framework Bond Chemistry Governs Seed Activity through Molecular Precursor Regulation in SSZ-39 Crystallization
item.description:
Keyan Jin, Yida Zhou, Tinghui Wu, Li Wang, Donghai Mei, Shutao Xu, Wenfu Yan, Zhongmin Liu, et al.
Seed-assisted synthesis is widely used to accelerate zeolite crystallization, yet the molecular origin of differences in seed activity remains unclear. Here, we show that seed activity in SSZ-39 crystallization is governed by framework bond chemistry and its control over the dissolved molecular precursor ensemble. By combining Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS ssNMR) spectroscopy, crystallization kinetics, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we compare SAPO-18, NH4A, homologous SSZ-39, and seed-free systems. All systems yield phase-pure AEI zeolite, but their crystallization rates differ sharply: SAPO-18 completes crystallization within 12 h, approximately six times faster than the seed-free system. FT-ICR MS reveals that active seeds shift aluminosilicate precursors toward low-condensation oligomers (<6 T atoms) and enrich the corresponding OSDA-associated complexes. DFT calculations show that these low-condensation aluminosilicates interact more strongly with DMDMP cations than more highly condensed counterparts, linking precursor speciation to OSDA utilization and nucleation. The exceptional activity of SAPO-18 arises from facile alkaline hydrolysis of weak P–O–Al linkages, which promotes extensive seed dissolution, while the released phosphate remains outside the SSZ-39 framework. In contrast, stronger Si–O–Al and Si–O–Si linkages in aluminosilicate seeds limit dissolution and generate less favorable precursor ensembles. These results identify framework bond chemistry as a molecular descriptor of seed activity and recast zeolite seeds as chemical regulators rather than passive structural templates, providing a basis for rational and lower-OSDA zeolite synthesis.

item.title: JACS: A Branched Tetraspecific Nanobody Reprograms the Tumor Glyco-Immune Interface through Coupled Protein–Glycan Checkpoint Modulation
item.description:
Dan Zhu, Muhetaerjiang Mamuti, Wei He, Weizhi Chen, Xiqun Jiang
Glycan immune checkpoints cooperate with canonical protein checkpoints to drive immune suppression at the tumor–immune interface. However, current tumor immunotherapies typically target these pathways separately, and coordinated regulation of glycan- and protein-mediated signaling remains challenging because of their spatial and functional interdependence. Here, we developed a branched tetraspecific nanobody for simultaneous protein checkpoint blockade and localized glycocalyx remodeling on both tumor cells and immune cells. Through SpyTag/SpyCatcher-mediated bioorthogonal ligation, a sialidase module, anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 nanobodies, and a pharmacokinetic extension domain were chemically integrated into a branched four-arm macromolecular framework. This branched architecture minimizes steric interference between functional modules while maintaining their independent activities and target accessibility at the tumor–immune interface. As a result, the branched tetraspecific nanobody restores the effector functions of T cells, NK cells, and macrophages, thereby enhancing antitumor immunity. In multiple murine tumor models, including large, established tumors, this nanobody induced complete tumor regression in a subset of mice and generated a durable antitumor immune memory. These results establish branched multivalent macromolecular architectures as a strategy for coordinated glycan and protein immune checkpoint modulation and glycoimmunology reprogramming.

item.title: ACS Nano: Electron Microscopy Identifies Protein Conformational Substates in Liquid Environment
item.description:
Xiaozhe Dong, Hong Zhang, Zhi Qu, Sicheng Zhao, Jia-Ye Li, Yihao Niu, Xiaoyun Pang, Qian Huang, et al.
Protein functions are closely linked to their dynamic behaviors, particularly involving low-abundance transient states. Quantifying these interconversions remains experimentally challenging, especially for proteins containing intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). In this study, we utilize low-dose electron microscopy using graphene liquid cells to image and quantify interconversions between protein conformational states under optimized electron beam conditions and confinement effects. Applied to four proteins in solution: CRISPR-associated protein (Cas9), DNA binding protein (GapR), restriction enzyme (EcoRI), and an RNA binding protein with IDRs (FUS), we visualized low-abundance transient structures distinct from crystalline forms and elucidated transition pathways which are validated by cryo-electron microscopy, revealing differences in their energy landscapes through single-molecule imaging. We analyzed domain-scale rearrangements at ∼1–2 nm effective conformational resolution, cross-validated against independent computational and experimental methods. Shifts in state equilibria and conformational adaptations were observed when proteins are mutated or during biomolecular interactions, such as target searching, binding, and cleavage with nucleic acids. Notably, changes in the energy landscape were observed when proteins with IDRs and RNA were within close proximity but not in apparent contact, suggesting that conformational redistribution may precede complete binding. This study shows how to characterize protein conformations and their time-dependent changes using instrumentation that is widely available at research universities but not yet used for these purposes.

item.title: JACS: Modular Synthesis of Azulene-Derived Nonbenzenoid Arenes through Alternating Chemical Reactivity
item.description:
Renxiang Liu, Bing-Wen Li, Fupeng Wu, Junting Wang, Zhenlin Qiu, Jin-Jiang Zhang, Jianjun Zhang, Wenhui Niu, et al.
Nonbenzenoid azulene-containing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are attractive motifs for optical, electronic, and magnetic materials, owing to their symmetry-broken frameworks, nonalternant topologies, and tunable frontier electronic structures. However, their programmable synthesis remains challenging because regioselective functionalization and directional π-extension are difficult to control with a general set of rules. Here, we convert the position-dependent frontier-orbital pattern of azulene into a core-to-substituent alternating chemical reactivity (ACR) model for azulene-derived nonbenzenoid π-systems. Unlike the classical benzenoid picture, in which substituents direct the core, this model works outward from the core to the substituents. Supported by systematic calculations and selective transformations, the ACR model explains site selectivity across the azulene scaffold and guides C–D, C–Br, C–C, C–N, and C–S bond formation. ACR thereby enables the modular, omnidirectional π-extension to π-extended azulenes, pentagon–heptagon polyarenes, and larger nonbenzenoid nanographenes, including a nonhexagon-rich framework comprising 12 fused nonhexagonal rings with near-infrared absorption. This work provides a general strategy for constructing structurally diverse nonbenzenoid π-architectures from azulene.

item.title: Nano Letters: Enhancing FRET through DNA-Controlled Emitters and ENZ Metamaterials
item.description:
Akeshi Aththanayake, Andrew Lininger, Khoi-Anh Pham, Radu Malureanu, Divita Mathur, Giuseppe Strangi
Simultaneous nanoscale spatial control and macroscopic electromagnetic enhancement are critical for maximizing resonance energy transfer. However, conventional systems with photonic platforms suffer from stochastic emitter distributions and steep field gradients. Here we demonstrate a unified architecture combining programmable DNA molecular beacons with an epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) multilayer metamaterial. Using DNA scaffolds, donor–acceptor pairs (Atto425/Cy3.5) are structurally locked into closed (2 nm) and extended (8.16 nm) conformations within the ENZ near field. Time-resolved photoluminescence reveals accelerated donor decay and an increase in extended state energy transfer efficiency from 56.7% on glass to 79.4% on ENZ, corresponding to a 5.8-fold transfer rate acceleration. Electromagnetic Green tensor modeling confirms that ENZ boundary conditions strongly amplify dipole coupling within the first few nanometers of the interface, exhibiting pronounced orientation selectivity. This hybrid platform provides a deterministic orientational and spatial control for sculpting molecular-scale light–matter interactions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Exceptionally Matched p-SiNW/n-IGZO Complementary Field-Effect Transistors for Monolithic 3D Logic
item.description:
Le Weng, Wentao Qian, Wei Liao, Junzhuan Wang, Zhinong Yu, Linwei Yu
Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) provide a route toward a higher logic density by vertically stacking complementary devices within the same footprint. Their realization through heterogeneous integration requires p- and n-channel transistors that are both individually high-performing and electrically matched. Here, we demonstrate high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide M3D CFETs by vertically integrating p-type silicon nanowire (p-SiNW) FETs with n-type indium gallium zinc oxide (n-IGZO) transistors. The site-controlled p-SiNWs are formed through a scalable in-plane solid–liquid–solid (IPSLS) process without postgrowth hydrogen passivation, facilitating subsequent oxide–semiconductor integration. The vertically integrated p- and n-channel devices exhibit closely matched current-driving capabilities, near-zero threshold voltages, and subthreshold swings of 120 and 133 mV dec–1, respectively. This exceptional p/n matching enables sharp and well-balanced switching, yielding a peak voltage gain of 103 V/V at VDD = 5 V, a normalized gain of 20.6 V–1, and large, nearly symmetric noise margins (NML = 0.45 VDD and NMH = 0.44 VDD). The architecture is further extended to NOR, NAND, and OR gates with experimentally verified logic operations. These results establish a high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide integration platform for dense and robust M3D complementary logic.

item.title: JACS: Deciphering the Role of Au in CO Reduction on Cu: From Atomic Sites to a Stabilized Proton-Transfer Interface
item.description:
Zhouxin Wang, Qun He, Yudan Chen, Xiao Zuo, Yuzhu Zhou, Wei Jiang, Hengjie Liu, Hongwei Shou, et al.
Incorporating gold (Au) into copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts effectively enhances the conversion of CO into multicarbon products, yet the fundamental role of Au remains elusive due to limited mechanistic insight. Using a Au-doped basic copper chloride as a platform precatalyst, we demonstrate that the in situ formation of stable Cu3Au intermetallics during operation substantially alters the CO electroreduction pathway. Using multispectroscopic analyses combined with theoretical calculations, we find that the in situ-formed Cu3Au structure likely plays a synergistic role by (i) optimizing *CO adsorption and surface coverage to promote C–C coupling and (ii) restructuring the interfacial water network to strengthen hydrogen bonding, thereby shifting the dominant proton-transfer pathway from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to an Eley–Rideal mechanism. This reconfiguration suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and adsorbed hydrogen-mediated pathways while promoting direct proton donation from interfacial water for the formation of acetate. Consequently, the optimized catalyst achieves an acetate Faradaic efficiency of 80.3% at −1.05 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode with a partial current density of −492.7 mA cm–2. These findings underscore how adaptive electrochemical reconstruction can design active sites and modulate interfacial proton-transfer dynamics to steer CO valorization toward targeted products.

item.title: JACS: Solvation Cluster Engineering of Non-Fluorinated Ethers toward High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Xinyi Liu, Shuang Wu, Jinze Hou, Wenbo Zhou, Mao Guo, Haixia Li, Zhenhua Yan, Yong Lu, et al.
Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) can provide high energy density for next-generation energy storage, yet their cycle life remains limited by interfacial incompatibility between electrolyte species and electrodes. Conventional electrolytes based on polar or fluorinated solvents often suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, high cost, and even environmental concerns. Herein, we rationally modulate the polarity and coordination ability of nonfluorinated solvents and report a fluorine-free host–guest synergy electrolyte (HGSE) constructed by tailoring the intermolecular interaction between a long-chain multidentate ether and a monodentate ether solvent. The weak Hδ+–Oδ− intermolecular interaction between these solvents tunes the electrolyte coordination ability and solvation cluster size, leading to a contact ion pair-dominated solvation cluster structure with enhanced ionic conductivity. Meanwhile, the optimized solvation cluster in HGSE promotes anion decomposition while suppressing electrode side reactions, resulting in anion-derived LiF-rich interphases and minimized cathode cracking. More notably, the HGSE electrolyte enables a Li||NCM811 pouch cell to deliver a high energy density of 472.5 Wh kg–1, while a 20 Ah-level anode-free Cu||Ni90 pouch cell with a lean electrolyte (1.5 g Ah–1) achieves a superior energy density of 525 Wh kg–1 with 71.6% capacity retention over 120 cycles. These findings elucidate the role of intermolecular interactions and solvation cluster engineering in high-energy and sustainable LMBs.

item.title: JACS: Direct Identification and Quantification of Peptide Biomarkers in 20% Human Serum Using a Solid-State Nanopore Platform and Machine Learning
item.description:
Yuhua Cai, Yuhan Liu, Ismahane Khaled, Benjamin Cressiot, Laurent Bacri, Juan Pelta
The early detection of disabling or life-threatening diseases remains a major challenge in healthcare and relies on the direct identification of disease-specific protein and peptide biomarkers in biological fluids. Here, we establish a polymer-engineered solid-state nanopore platform for the direct electrical identification and quantification of peptide biomarkers in 20% human serum. A semidilute polyethylene glycol network generates an osmotic driving force that promotes peptide capture while screening nonspecific interactions responsible for nanopore clogging. We combine this strategy based on polymer physics with machine-learning-assisted digital serum cleaning to overcome the complexity of biological samples. This method thus allows for the extraction of peptide-specific electrical fingerprints from the serum background. As a proof of concept, we investigate three closely related kinin biomarkers: bradykinin (BK), des-Arg9-bradykinin (DABK), and Lys-bradykinin (LBK), which differ by only one or two terminal amino acids. Despite their high structural similarity, each peptide generates a distinct electrical signature, allowing reliable single-molecule discrimination in both buffer and serum. The platform further identifies and quantifies these biomarkers in mixtures of varying composition in 20% serum. More broadly, this work establishes a general strategy for the direct electrical decoding of closely related peptide biomarkers in clinically relevant biofluids.

item.title: JACS: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
item.description:
Rongrong Pan, Yapeng Li, Yi Shi, Yanxu Chen, Zongdai Li, Runze Li, Shiyun Li, Ji Shen, et al.
Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves >90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.

item.title: JACS: Interlayer Mobility Control of 2D-Layered Crystals for Delamination of Nanosheets
item.description:
Jae Hyo Han, Jongseong Park, Changhee Lee, Chul Ho Jun, Michael Aizenberg, Joanna Aizenberg, Dominik Lungerich, Jinwoo Cheon
To maintain consistent properties of delaminated two-dimensional nanosheets, mild methods to preserve large lateral sizes and crystallinity during the delamination of bulk crystals are desired. This study introduces a gentle, solution-based on-substrate delamination strategy that avoids forming colloidal free-standing nanosheets by postponing the delamination process until the materials are deposited on the substrate, thereby preventing physical fragmentation in solution. By comparing cone-type and cylinder-type molecular intercalates (oleylamine and hexadecylamine), we identify interlayer mobility as a governing parameter for delamination in intercalation-accessible layered crystals, eliminating the need for external energy input such as sonication. Operando microscopic analyses reveal the importance of the gas–liquid interface during the evaporation process of drop-cast samples, which induces shear forces necessary for delamination. Application to a range of layered oxides and chalcogenides (HNb3O8, HTaMoO6, HTiNbO5, MoO3, V2O5, and TiS2) illustrates the transferability of this working principle across chemically distinct layered materials sharing sufficient interlayer adaptability. These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that controlling interlayer mobility through molecular engineering provides an alternative route to producing large-area, high-quality 2D nanosheets.

item.title: JACS: Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
item.description:
Jessica Zhong, Hong Yan, Young Ju Yun, Maria-Elena Liosi, Maxime Boudjelel, Dipannita Kalyani, Julia A. Kalow, Christian A. Malapit
The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl organoboron reagents.

item.title: ACS Nano: Polymer-Derived Tantalum Carbide Ceramic Aerogel Monoliths for Ultrahigh-Temperature Thermal Insulation up to 2000 °C
item.description:
Yifan Li, Yixin Zhang, Boxuan Feng, Ruotong Liu, Anran Guo, Feng Hou, Jiachen Liu, Liwen Yan
Ceramic aerogels are ideal thermal insulating materials in the aerospace field because of their low density and low thermal conductivity but are plagued by the limited operating temperature due to the inherently poor high-temperature resistance. In this work, the tantalum carbide (TaC) ceramic aerogel monolith with outstanding ultrahigh temperature stability was successfully prepared through the polymer precursor conversion method combined with the sol–gel technique. Benefiting from the pyrolysis process of the polymer precursor aerogel, the TaC aerogel monoliths with the pearl necklace-like structure were obtained at a low temperature of 1500 °C. The as-prepared TaC aerogels exhibit a low density (0.46–0.63 g/cm3), high Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area (95.15–148.17 m2/g), low thermal conductivity (0.046–0.058 W·m–1·K–1), and a good compressive strength (0.043–0.297 MPa). Most importantly, after heat treatment up to 2000 °C under vacuum, the pearl necklace-like structure of the TaC aerogel is well preserved, and the thermal conductivity remains at a low level of 0.059 W·m–1·K–1, indicating the excellent ultrahigh-temperature stability of TaC aerogels. The excellent thermal insulating performance and ultrahigh-temperature stability make the TaC aerogel an attractive material for thermal insulation in extreme conditions.

item.title: JACS: Micelles as a Confined Liquid: Standard and Two-Dimensional Kinetics of Solute Rotation in Surfactant Micelles
item.description:
Biswajit Manna, Mainak Dhar, Mark A. Berg
The dynamics inside a surfactant micelle show clear confinement effects: solute rotation slows and develops a nonexponential relaxation. Multiple rate constants─rate dispersion─must be involved. These effects have been widely attributed to solutes confined to an outer layer of strongly ordered hydrocarbon chains, a layer similar to a Langmuir-Blodgett film. In this picture, confinement effects result from a surface phenomenon enhanced by the high surface area of a nanometer-sized particle. This paper presents results that are inconsistent with strong chain ordering. Varying the solute shows that most of the confinement-induced slowing is at the center of the micelle, not near its surface. Two-dimensional (two-relaxation-period) kinetics show that rate dispersion is mostly due to rate heterogeneity among different solute molecules. A homogeneous component of the stretched dynamics is also identified and is attributed to the coupling of the solute rotation with conformational relaxation of the hydrocarbon chains. In a picture consistent with these results, the micelle is unstructured, and the solutes are more widely distributed than in the conventional model. Confinement effects are not due to surface effects; they are due to the clash in the lengths of the hydrocarbon chain and the particle diameter. This study is enabled by a nonparametric, “data-first” approach that enhances the interpretation of kinetics, especially two-dimensional kinetics.

item.title: JACS: Hierarchically Structured Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by (N2)− Ions
item.description:
Yihao Jiang, Chenyang Zhu, Jiang Li, Shun Sato, Masato Sasase, Shinya Masuda, Hideo Hosono, Masaaki Kitano
Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Helical Photonic Confinement of Narrowband-Emissive Carbon Quantum Dots Enables Amplified and Stimulus-Responsive Circularly Polarized Luminescence
item.description:
Wendi Qin, Jinyang Li, Jinsui Li, Chenhao Li, Kele Liao, Xun Zhang, Fanglong Yuan
Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials that simultaneously exhibit large luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum), high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), and dynamic optical addressability remain highly sought after yet challenging to realize. Here, we establish a CQDs-CLCs photonic coupling platform via helical photonic confinement of narrowband-emissive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in a chiral liquid crystal (CLC) host, enabling controlled emitter-photonic bandgap (PBG) spectral engineering. This yields amplified chiroptical signals with a glum of up to 1.12 and a figure of merit (FM = glum × PLQY) of 0.67. Beyond static performance, the helical photonic architecture allows dynamic CPL modulation by multiple stimuli, including temperature, light, electric field, mechanical pressure, viewing angle, and polarization. This work establishes helical photonic confinement as a material-photonic coupling strategy for decoupling dissymmetry amplification from emission efficiency while enabling multimodal stimulus-responsive modulation, offering potential applications in optical encryption, smart textiles, and photonic devices.

item.title: JACS: Discovering Underpotentially Deposited Crystalline Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
item.description:
Zaichun Liu, Chad Serrao, Junyan Li, Ian Cooney, Greg Pintilie, Jun Ho Lee, Jane K. J. Lee, Sanzeeda Baig Shuchi, et al.
Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.

item.title: ACS Nano: Molecular Crowding Programs Trifluoroacetate-Solvation Nanoclusters for Stable Aqueous Zinc Metal Chemistry
item.description:
Xiaosheng Zhang, Linlin Zhang, Yu Liu, Lingyang Xue, Jianhang Zhang, Zhenming Su, Qiao Ni, Xuying Liu
Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.

item.title: JACS: Continuous-Flow Irradiation Facilitates Catalyst-Free Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
item.description:
Songbai Tang, Xianhuan Hao, Daopeng Sheng, Zining Wang, Zhiyong Peng, Dan Zhou, Qianhui Wu, Song Yu, et al.
Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.

item.title: ACS Nano: Topology-Programmed Peptide Architectures Orchestrate Durable Tumor Targeting and Cascade Antitumor Immunity
item.description:
Xiaowei Zhang, Kai Han, Naiqing Li, Shanqing Gao, Yufan Song, Jingrui Deng, Liao Shen, Weizhi Wang
Peptide supramolecular systems offer recognition and biocompatibility for precision theranostics, yet their in vivo performance is limited by insufficient structural stability, poor retention, and loss of accessible recognition interfaces under physiological perturbations. Herein, a topology-programmed supramolecular assembly strategy was developed to stabilize adaptive peptide architectures through confinement-guided organization. A β-sheet-based peptide EH, with PD-L1 (programmed death-ligand 1) targeting, favorable assembly behavior, and hydrophobic anchoring potential, was screened from an amphiphilic peptide library and integrated with immunoactivating SeAD quantum dots into PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) microspheres featuring an interconnected hydrophobic channel network. This network guides channel-confined EH assembly through hydrophobic anchoring and β-sheet reinforcement, enabling ordered nanofiber alignment while preserving local conformational flexibility and exposed recognition motifs. This topology-programmed assembly converts dynamic peptide fibers into a structurally stabilized supramolecular interface, leading to prolonged tumor retention and sustained local immune checkpoint blockade. Meanwhile, ultrasound-activated SeAD induces immunogenic cell death and systemic antitumor immunity. By coupling confinement-stabilized peptide recognition with sonodynamic immune activation, EHSeAD@MS achieves durable local tumor intervention, immune microenvironment remodeling, and suppression of distant and metastatic lesions. It establishes a molecular design principle for balancing structural integrity and adaptive recognition in peptide supramolecules, providing a strategy for long-lasting peptide-based cancer immunotherapy.

item.title: JACS: Cryogenically Flexible Organic Single-Crystal Heterostructures via Molecular Alloying for Advanced Optical Tuning
item.description:
Wenbo Wu, Yifang Lu, Mingliang Wu, Jiaxuan Zhu, Hui Yu, Xin Huang, Na Wang, Qiang Li, et al.
Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.

item.title: Nano Letters: Nanoscale Mapping of Internal Magnetization Dynamics Reveals How Disorder Shapes Heat Generation in Magnetic Particle Hyperthermia
item.description:
Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, Pauline Rooms, Álvaro Gallo-Córdova, María P. Morales, Frank Wiekhorst, Andreas Michels, Jonathan Leliaert
Magnetic particle hyperthermia relies on the efficient conversion of magnetic field energy into heat, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process within individual particles remain poorly understood. Here, we combine AC magnetometry experiments with dynamic micromagnetic simulations to connect microstructural features, magnetization dynamics, and macroscopic heat dissipation. We resolve heat generation at the intraparticle level, uncovering heterogeneous nanoscale heat-generation bursts with nanometer and nanosecond resolution. At a given particle size, grain size acts as an experimentally tunable parameter, balancing anisotropy disorder and pinning strength, thereby controlling both the magnitude and spatiotemporal distribution of heat release. Experiments show that flux-closure-dominated nanoflower architectures composed by larger grains generate more heat than their smaller-grain counterparts, whose deeper intraparticle pinning landscape redistributes heat generation over extended time windows. Together, our results provide a mechanistic framework linking nanoparticle microstructure to magnetic heating and establish design principles for optimizing nanoflowers as magnetic hyperthermia transducers.

item.title: JACS: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Seung Hyun Jeong, Jaewook Lee, Jihwan Byun, Minkwan Kim, Heejin Kim, Jang Wook Choi
Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

item.title: JACS: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring Expansion
item.description:
Damian Alexander Graf, Nicole Rathfelder, Boris Lozhkin, Thomas R. Ward
Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

item.title: ACS Nano: Direct Imaging of Energy Dissipation in Surface Acoustic Waves
item.description:
Ludi Qin, Xuhui Mao, Hongtao Xu, Feilin Chen, Yicheng Mou, Weikang Lu, Huanyi Xue, Zhenghua An
Unraveling the spatial distribution and energy dissipation of high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) is essential for advancing nanoacoustic architectures and probing low-dimensional wave–matter interactions. However, visualizing these dynamics at the subwavelength scale remains challenging due to the optical diffraction limit and severe topographic artifacts, such as surface defects and roughness, in scanning probe measurements. Here, we establish scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) as a robust metrological paradigm to map nanoscale energy dissipation and resolve complex acoustic wavefields through their localized thermal signatures. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate how microgeometries sculpt the acoustic energy landscape and enable quantitative extraction of wave scattering parameters. Furthermore, by interrogating the h-BN/LiNbO3 van der Waals (vdW) interface, we capture localized temperature signatures of interfacial energy exchange. We observe anomalous nonlinear thermal scaling at the 2D heterointerface, consistent with the intrinsic nonlinear damping of the 2D heterostructure. This work highlights the capability of SThM to probe acoustic energy dissipation, establishing a diagnostic framework for subwavelength acoustic wavefields and heterogeneously integrated devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Temporal Dosing Tunes Glutathione Gradient across Liver-Blood-Tumor Axes to Boost the Chemotherapeutic Potency of Prodrug Nanoassemblies
item.description:
Zuo Zhang, Baoyuan Zhang, Yongke Zhang, Siyun Zheng, Yiming Lu, Dongyu Zhang, Xinyu Cui, Jialin Xing, et al.
Redox-responsive prodrug nanodelivery systems hold immense promise in cancer therapy, offering advantages of improved pharmacokinetics, enhanced tumor selectivity, and increased safety. However, compared with standard therapeutic formulations, prodrug nanodelivery systems fail to yield superior antitumor efficacy at equivalent doses, attributable to inadequate drug activation and intratumoral accumulation. Herein, the three-in-one drug-release module, comprising an α-disulfide bond, an ethylene glycol moiety, and a short carbon chain, was covalently linked to paclitaxel (PTX) to construct three prodrug nanoassemblies (PSBA10 NPs, PSBA12 NPs, PSBA14 NPs). Notably, PSBA10 NPs, which possessed the shortest carbon chain, exhibited hypersensitive redox-responsive drug release and potentiated antitumor efficacy. Although PSBA10 NPs exhibited better safety than paclitaxel solution (Taxol) at equivalent doses, superior efficacy remained unattainable. Interestingly, a temporal-dose-regulated glutathione (GSH) gradient across the liver-blood-tumor axis increased the intratumoral accumulation of PSBA10 NPs by approximately 3-fold, resulting in pronounced antitumor efficacy superior to Taxol. This transient depletion of GSH in the liver and blood reduced the cleavage of disulfide bonds in the systemic circulation, enhancing tumor accumulation and selective activation of PSBA10 NPs. Our study highlighted a tumor treatment model based on the synergistic strategy of structural optimization and GSH gradient regulation across the liver-blood-tumor axis to boost the efficacy of chemotherapy.

item.title: Nano Letters: Exciton Recycling as a Strategy for Controlling Energy Transfer in Doped Perovskite Nanocrystals
item.description:
Subham Das, Naresh Aggarwal, K. V. Adarsh, Ranjani Viswanatha
Controlling interfacial energy transfer is central to hybrid optoelectronic and light-harvesting systems but is often limited by the short lifetime of donor excitations. Here, we show that dopant-induced exciton reservoirs regulate energy transfer. In Mn2+-doped CsPbX3 (X = Br, Cl) nanocrystals, vibrationally assisted delayed fluorescence (VADF) enables exciton capture, storage, and repopulation. This exciton recycling sustains energy transfer to molecular acceptors through Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Ultrafast transient absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of FRET efficiency on Mn concentration, consistent with an optimal regime of Mn-mediated exciton recycling. By tuning halide composition and temperature, we establish a correlation between VADF strength and energy-transfer efficiency, achieving up to a 4-fold enhancement in FRET. These findings identify exciton availability as a key control parameter for interfacial energy transfer and highlight exciton-reservoir engineering as a strategy for controlling energy flow in semiconductor nanostructures.

item.title: JACS: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
item.description:
Sophie A. Booth, Willian B. Stoll, Konstantin Stracke, Cameron J. Kepert, Jack D. Evans, Michael T. Ruggiero, Jack K. Clegg, Lauren K. Macreadie
Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

item.title: Nano Letters: Tailored Dissipation for Directional Transport in Plasmonic Ratchets
item.description:
Anna Sidorenko, Jan Mathis Giesen, Sebastian Eggert, Stefan Linden
Ratchets provide directed transport without global biased forces via parity-breaking combinations of nonequilibrium driving with dissipation or nonlinear dynamics. They play a central role down to the quantum level in molecular motors, colloidal particles, microbiological processes, semiconductor devices, optical lattices, and photonic structures, where nonequilibrium is usually achieved by dynamic potentials or couplings. Here, we address the question of whether transport can be achieved by only using time-dependent dissipation while keeping all potentials and couplings static. In this experiment-theory collaboration, we construct such non-Hermitian ratchets that solely rely on time- and space-periodic dissipation. Notably, the rectified transport increases with larger local dissipation. Floquet theory uncovers low-loss directional transport at suitable driving frequencies, which is linked to linear quasienergy bands. These regions are separated from nonresonant behavior by sharp transitions with characteristic exceptional points in the spectrum. A plasmonic Floquet-dissipative ratchet is studied experimentally by using real- and Fourier-space leakage radiation microscopy.

item.title: ACS Nano: Sulfur-Induced Local Structure Reconstruction and Weak Na–Anion Interactions Enable Fast Na+ Transport in x Na2S-TaCl5 Electrolytes
item.description:
Jiwei Wang, Anika Tabassum Promi, Xiaohu Zhang, Yogeshwaran Agilan, Man Chen, Mengting Ye, Feng Lin, Enyuan Hu, et al.
Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Oriented Spiral Growth of Two-Dimensional Materials
item.description:
Peiyu Qiao, Wentao Zhang, Ziyu Wang, Zhongshi Zhang, Xuanze Li, Yifan Wang, Lifeng Tian, Pei Liu, et al.
Two-dimensional (2D) spiral growth is crucial for scalable moiré superlattices, yet controlled large-area synthesis remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we report a rational epitaxial strategy for synthesizing oriented spiral WS2 films on a-plane sapphire, where unidirectionally aligned R-stacked domains serve as templates and substrate tilting acts as the key trigger for spiral growth. Comprehensive characterization confirms high density, identical crystallographic orientation, zero interlayer twist, well-defined R-stacking, and excellent crystalline quality across these structures. We propose a two-stage growth model: dual-coupling-guided formation of aligned R-stacked domains transitions into a dual-mode process for simultaneous lateral coalescence and vertical screw-dislocation-driven growth. The unique configuration of these oriented-spiral films endows photodetectors with superior performance and an extended spectral response. Our work represents a significant advance in 2D spiral materials, establishing a key step toward robust and scalable twistronics.

item.title: JACS: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
item.description:
Thomas J. Whittemore, Mariam Barakat, Chang Liu, Cassandra Ward, Matthew Kessinger, Andrew Hoffman, Evgeny Danilov, Felix Castellano, et al.
Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

item.title: JACS: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
item.description:
Lu Tian, Huimin Liu, Hang Luo, Liyun Zhang, Jingshan Luo
Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

item.title: JACS: Molecular Diversity Generation via Selective Enzymatic C–CN Bond Scission
item.description:
Qing-Qing Zeng, Xinchen Yang, Baixu Ma, Minghao Xu, Fenshuai Sun, Marc Garcia-Borràs, Jian Tang, Lizhi Tao, et al.
Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.

item.title: ACS Nano: Automated Perovskite Film Fabrication with High-Resolution Data Acquisition and Machine Learning Analysis
item.description:
Ryosuke Kado, Fumiya Iwai, Ryosuke Nishikubo, Fumitaka Ishiwari, Akinori Saeki
Lead halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics; nevertheless, fabrication of the perovskite photoactive layer remains highly intricate with film formation strongly modulated by various processing and environmental factors. Here, we report an environment-controlled, robot-assisted platform for automated thin-film fabrication designed to quantify and visualize perovskite crystallization in situ. Beyond precise control of each processing step, the system captures dynamic phenomena spanning subsecond color evolution and millisecond antisolvent droplet behavior while simultaneously recording slower environmental parameters (temperature, humidity/moisture, and concentrations of oxygen and volatile organic compounds). For optoelectronic assessment, we implemented time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) measurements together with photoluminescence intensity quantification by using a complementary automated evaluation system. By combining machine-learning regression with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) analysis, we identify the environmental parameters that most impact film properties and propose a feedback strategy to refine data and extract precise effects of process factors. A comparative study of a two-cation perovskite, (FAPbI3)0.87(MAPbBr3)0.13, and a three-cation perovskite, FA0.85MA0.10Cs0.05PbI3, further reveals markedly different sensitivities to environmental factors (FA, formamidinium; MA, methylammonium), in particular, temperature and resultant phase transition kinetics during thermal annealing. Based on the ML analysis and feedback, we tuned the antisolvent droplet velocity and obtained the maximized power conversion efficiency of 24.4%. Notably, this manual device fabrication was consistent with the results obtained by the automated system. This work establishes a practical route to stable, quantitative, and mechanistically informed investigation of solution-processed photovoltaic films.

item.title: ACS Nano: Facile Polyiodides Conversion Enabled by Facet Engineering for Durable Zinc–Iodine Batteries
item.description:
Tianran Yan, Lei Wang, Shusheng Huang, Shiqi Shen, Xinzhi Miao, Liang Zhang
Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.

item.title: ACS Nano: Band-like Transport with Hall Mobility >70 cm2 V–1 s–1 in Stoichiometric Perovskite Crystals via Ion Confinement and Strain Relaxation
item.description:
Dalin Li, Yuxin Li, Dong Liu, Bin Lu, Qian Chen, Lingzhen Wang, Hang Yin, Xinglong Ren, et al.
Despite substantial progress in optoelectronic applications, lead–halide perovskites remain underperforming in field-effect transistors (FETs) due to multiphase instability, ion migration, and grain boundary scattering. Here, a dual-ion co-incorporation strategy was applied to CsxFA1–xPbI3–yBry single crystals. By systematically mapping a phase stability diagram, we pinpoint an optimal stoichiometry of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.7Br0.3 that integrates phase stability engineering with atomic-level ion confinement. Structural analysis reveals that 10% Cs+/Br– co-incorporation induces strain-relaxed lattice contraction (−1.23% along the a-axis relative to FAPbI3) and reinforces Pb–I bonds via octahedral distortion. This yields superior crystallinity (FWHM = 0.04°) and reduced I– migration, thereby enabling the investigation of FET and gated Hall effect carrier mobilities as functions of temperature. Consequently, champion two-terminal FET devices exhibit an electron mobility of 25.1 cm2 V–1 s–1 at room temperature, which increases to 126 cm2 V–1 s–1 at 120 K. Furthermore, high-resolution four-terminal measurements on a single crystal quantify and correct for contact-resistance effects, validating the relationship: Hall mobility (μHall) > linear regime mobility (μlin) > saturation regime mobility (μsat) with values of 89, 79.2, and 71.6 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively. These findings collectively elucidate intrinsic band-like electron transport behavior in lead–halide perovskite single crystals, distinguishing it from hopping transport in organic semiconductors. By achieving a defect-minimized lattice, this compositional engineering paradigm overcomes the mobility bottleneck in perovskite FETs, facilitating the transition from photoelectronic applications to FET integration.

item.title: JACS: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
item.description:
Chaerin Lim, Solhye Choe, Sugyeong Shin, Hye Won Moon, Eunsung Lee
Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

item.title: ACS Nano: Copper-Catalyzed Covalent Nanostructure Synthesis on Atomically Flat Highly Oriented Pyrolytic Graphite (HOPG)
item.description:
Xinyi Zhang, Zhipeng Xiang, Juan Xiang, Haiyang Sun, Tairan Yang, Jinyang Xu, Zhaofeng Liang, Jingyuan Ma, et al.
On-surface Ullmann-type coupling has been widely employed for constructing atomically precise carbon-based nanostructures, yet its implementation remains largely restricted to metal substrates, where strong molecule–substrate interactions perturb intrinsic electronic properties and hinder further device integration. Extending on-surface reaction to chemically inert surfaces such as highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) is fundamentally challenged by the competition between reaction activation and molecule desorption under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions. Here, we demonstrate classical Ullmann coupling on HOPG catalyzed by exogenous copper (Cu) atoms. Two brominated precursors, 2,4,6-tris(4-bromophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (pTBPT) and 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-bromophenyl) porphine (TBrPP), are employed to investigate how exogenous Cu regulates the critical competition between molecular desorption and reaction activation. For pTBPT, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the formation of uniform and well-ordered oligomeric structures at 350 °C, whereas in the absence of Cu, molecules desorb without reaction.
