Synchrotron radiation X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (SR-XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further indicate that Cu atoms simultaneously promote molecular anchoring and reduce the activation barrier for dehalogenative coupling. As a complementary system, STM and XPS analysis of TBrPP reveals a critical competition between molecular desorption and dehalogenative coupling. While HR-XPS reveals in situ metalation at room temperature, STM imaging confirms that complete molecular desorption occurs at 200 °C, preventing subsequent dehalogenative coupling. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how transition metal mediates the interplay between surface reaction and desorption, while offering a strategy for the fabrication of structurally defined covalent nanostructures on electronically decoupled platforms.

item.title: ACS Nano: A Hyaluronic Acid-Stabilized Zinc-Loaded Probiotic Mitigates Nanoplastic Toxicity across the Microbiota–Gut–Brain Axis
item.description:
Jing Zhao, Ke Zhang, Yimeng Fang, Runchao Tao, Huaibiao Xu, Jia Yi, Hong Yu, Rongbing Chen, et al.
Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut–immune–brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions. In zebrafish chronically exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics, we observe reproducible neurobehavioral impairment coupled with inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, barrier stress, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and multiorgan histopathology. ZG@EcN@HA yields the most coherent rescue compared with single-component controls, restoring behavioral outputs and realigning immune–redox–neurochemical readouts. ASV-based profiling shows recovery of microbial diversity and a shift toward a control-like community structure, including reduced dominance of inflammation-linked taxa. Intestinal transcriptomics and integrative correlation analyses further support normalization of barrier/metabolic programs and attenuation of innate inflammatory signaling. Together, the data identify a materials-enabled strategy for microbiota–gut–brain protection against chronic nanoplastic stress.

item.title: JACS: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
item.description:
Anna Iniutina, Santanu Ghosh, Nobuya Tsuji, Chandra Kanta De, Benjamin List
Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dopant Engineered Y-Doped Hafnia-Zirconia Nanolaminates with 0.26 nm Equivalent Oxide Thickness for Dynamic Random Access Memory Capacitors
item.description:
Jonghoon Shin, Haengha Seo, Tae Kyun Kim, Sung Keun Shim, Hyun Wook Kim, Heewon Paik, Haewon Song, Seong Jae Shin, et al.
Y-doped Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 demonstrated feasible field-induced ferroelectric properties for capacitor dielectrics in dynamic random access memory (DRAM) by stepwise cycling, which enabled low-voltage charge boosting. However, practical implementation remains limited by high cycling stress and leakage current density (J) degradation. This study reported a Y-doped ZrO2/HfO2/ZrO2 nanolaminate with middle-inserted and top-inserted Y2O3 layers, enabling low-voltage charge boosting with substantially decreased stepwise cycling stress. This effect arose from a more uniform distribution of oxygen-vacancy-dopant complexes, thereby decreasing the energy barrier for the tetragonal-to-polar orthorhombic phase transition. The middle-inserted Y2O3 layer underwent substitutional diffusion, stabilized the tetragonal phase and suppressed J by acceptor doping. In contrast, the top-inserted Y2O3 layer displayed limited bulk diffusion, resulting in minimal lattice strain and phase change, but further suppressed J. Consequently, a 5.2 nm-thick film achieved an ultralow equivalent oxide thickness of ∼0.26 nm while satisfying the DRAM J criterion (J < 10–7 A cm–2 at ±0.8 V), outperforming all previously reported DRAM dielectrics.

item.title: Nano Letters: Shear Assisted Diamond Formation in Cold-Compressed HOPG
item.description:
Brock M. Nicholas, Alan G. Salek, Ines F. Vaz, Hendrik Heimes, Xingshuo Huang, Jessica Wierbik, Samuel R. B. Case, Jodie E. Bradby, et al.
Diamond synthesis from a graphite precursor is primarily constrained by the requirement for the simultaneous application of extreme pressures and temperatures. We explore the microstructural changes in highly oriented pyrolytic graphite subject to shear during room temperature compression. Using a diamond anvil cell, nonhydrostatic pressures of up to 160 GPa were applied, resulting in an optically transparent, diamond-like material above 80 GPa that reverted to an opaque, largely graphite-like material upon decompression. Detailed microstructural analysis of the recovered sample revealed nanoscale diamond-like domains embedded within a graphitic matrix containing shear bands and localized basal slip features consistent with a high shear environment. Employing a rotational diamond anvil cell greatly enhanced these shear-induced features, producing significant amounts of diamond in samples recovered from applied pressures as low as 15 GPa. These findings demonstrate that shear can facilitate the graphite-to-diamond transformation, enabling sp3 bond formation under conditions where extreme temperatures are not required.

item.title: ACS Nano: Oxygen-Promoted Dehydrogenation on Size-Selected Cu–Pd Pentamer Clusters for Low-Temperature Hydrogen Release from Cyclic Hydrocarbons
item.description:
Mykhailo Vaidulych, Yonghyuk Lee, Federico Loi, Petr Vitek, Michael Vorochta, Stanislav Valtera, Ivan Khalakhan, Claudia de Melo, et al.
Despite extensive studies on cycloalkane and cycloalkene dehydrogenation for liquid organic hydrogen carrier applications, the mechanisms governing selective H2 release under mild conditions remain poorly understood. Here, subnanometer CuxPdy pentamer clusters supported on ZrO2 represent a highly active and selective class of low-temperature dehydrogenation catalysts. Pd5 exhibits the highest benzene and molecular H2 formation rates from dehydrogenation of cyclohexene, followed by Cu2Pd3 and Cu3Pd2, whereas Cu5 is inactive. All active catalysts favored H2 over H2O as the hydrogen-containing product and completely suppressed combustion pathways, with no detectable CO2 formation. Oxygen-lean conditions further favored H2 formation across all active catalysts, with H2 selectivity exceeding 99% for Pd5. Kinetic analysis of Cu3Pd2 reveals positive fractional apparent orders in both C6H10 and O2 and an effective apparent activation energy of approximately 66 kJ·mol–1, while reactant composition and temperature systematically control H2/H2O branching. In situ XPS and in situ GIWAXS reveal that catalytic activity and cluster stability arise from the interplay of atomic composition, electronic structure, metal–oxygen interactions, and the chemical environment, with Cu exhibiting a composition-sensitive redox response and Pd-containing clusters accommodating oxygen while retaining electronically active Pd-derived states near the Fermi level. DFT/MLIP free-energy calculations identify kinetically accessible O-assisted first C–H activation pathways involving H transfer to cluster-bound O, with barriers strongly dependent on cluster composition and O configuration. These findings establish an ensemble-based structure–activity framework for controlling dehydrogenation pathways and provide design principles for catalysts that efficiently promote selective hydrogen release suitable for hydrogen carrier applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: When Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Twist: Opportunities for Spintronics and Quantum Technologies
item.description:
Tuan Dung Nguyen, Thi Hoa Hoang, Bao Tung Hop Nguyen, Duc Trong Bui, Duc Truong Dinh, Quynh Huong Nguyen, Minh Hoang Dam, Kostya S Novoselov, et al.
Moiré superlattices form quantum-active interfaces in which geometric reconstruction of stacked two-dimensional (2D) materials generates emergent quantum phases that are not present in the parent materials. These engineered interfaces give rise to a wide range of quantum phenomena, including strongly correlated electronic states, flat-band formation, topological phases of matter, and spin–valley locking, all of which can be tuned in situ through the twist angle. Twisted hetero/homostructures of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) exhibit an unprecedented degree of control over electronic and spin degrees of freedom, driving rapid advances in the emerging field of twistronics and opening pathways toward next-generation spintronic device applications. In this Review, we examine the fundamental concepts, applications, and prospects of twisted 2D TMDs. We outline the evolution from three-dimensional (3D) to 2D materials and the concept of twistronics, then highlight the emergent structural and magnetic properties of twisted 2D TMDs and their heterostructures. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future directions toward applications in spintronic and quantum technologies.

item.title: JACS: Living Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for Efficient Light-Driven CO2-to-Chemical Conversion
item.description:
Jing Li, Jicong Zhang, Zhangfeng Yu, Zehao Zhang, Hongyu Chen, Junfeng Shen, Yi Liu, Zhiyong Zhang, et al.
Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.

item.title: ACS Nano: Centrosymmetry Breaking of Cobalt–Vanadium-Layered Double Hydroxide Nanosheets via Nitrogen Doping for Enhanced Piezocatalytic Tumor Therapy
item.description:
Chaojie Yu, Yu Yang, Tao Wang, Ruimin Xue, Shibo Wang, Yanfang Zhu, Yajie Zhang, Tingting Hu, et al.
Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising tumor therapeutic strategy because it enables oxygen-independent generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS) with deep tissue penetration. However, the piezocatalytic efficiency of piezoelectric nanomaterials remains constrained by limited lattice distortion, low carrier separation efficiency, and insufficient catalytic active sites. Herein, we report the centrosymmetry breaking of cobalt–vanadium-layered double hydroxide (CoV-LDH) nanosheets via nitrogen doping for efficient ultrasound (US)-mediated piezocatalytic tumor therapy. Owing to the nitrogen doping-induced disruption of the centrosymmetric structure and lattice distortion in CoV-LDH, nitrogen-doped CoV-LDH (N-CoV-LDH) achieves an ultrahigh piezoelectric coefficient of 89.4 pm·V–1, which is superior to that of previously reported piezocatalytic nanomaterials. Moreover, nitrogen doping introduces an unsaturated coordination environment, significantly promoting the adsorption and activation of O2 (Eads = −2.63 eV) and H2O (Eads = −2.37 eV), thereby enhancing piezocatalytic redox reaction kinetics (k > 1.1 × 103 min–1·g–1). Consequently, under low-power US stimulation (0.15 W·cm–2), N-CoV-LDH nanosheets exhibit markedly enhanced ROS generation efficiency, including that of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), superoxide anions (·O2–), and singlet oxygen (1O2). This robust piezocatalytic ROS generation induces tumor cell apoptosis and immunogenic cell death, thereby activating an antitumor immune response characterized by dendritic cell maturation, M1 macrophage polarization, and T cell activation. Ultimately, N-CoV-LDH-mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieves suppression rates of 97.78% for primary tumors and 87.67% for metastatic tumors, establishing an efficient therapeutic paradigm for suppressing tumor metastasis and recurrence.

item.title: JACS: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
item.description:
Zirui Lv, Minchao Liu, Yi Yang, Wenyuan Hu, Wenyu Yang, Yijin Wang, Qiutong Li, Fengyang Liu, et al.
Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

item.title: JACS: Assisted Tandem Catalysis with M–M Bonded Heterobimetallic Pd–Pt Complexes: Accessing Both Pd and Pt Catalytic Cycles
item.description:
James L. Corey, Taytum O. S. Hilton, Joshua J. Whipple, Alyssa N. Merrill, T. L. Angus Lam, Joshua D. Hansen, E. Ohana Shepley, Stacey J. Smith, et al.
We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. These bimetallic complexes act as a reservoir for catalytically active Pd and Pt centers, and catalysis is observed in a variety of Pd- and Pt-catalyzed reactions. We demonstrate that tandem catalytic reactions with our Pd(I)/Pt(I) complex can capitalize on both Pd and Pt catalytic cycles to enable multistep processes. These include tandem hydrosilylation/Hiyama coupling, Suzuki coupling/amide reduction, Buchwald–Hartwig amination/amide reduction, and Heck coupling/amide reduction. Tandem cycloisomerization/Heck coupling is also observed with our Pd(I)/Pt(III) complex. Control studies demonstrate that homobimetallic Pd–Pd and Pt–Pt complexes do not perform the tandem catalytic reactions and that the Pd–Pt complex is stable under air and moisture for at least 9 months. The M–M bond in these complexes enables access to unique Pd and Pt oxidation states and facilitates M–M communication, both of which can have an impact during catalysis.

item.title: JACS: Pressure-Induced Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Dimerization and Irreversible Optical Reconstruction in a 2D Hybrid Lead Halide
item.description:
Xiaofan Xu, Hao Yu, Jiang Han, Zewei Quan
External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ion Transport Enhancement in Charge-Regulating Hydrogels
item.description:
Pierre J. Walker, David Beyer, Christian Holm, Zhen-Gang Wang
Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this nonmonotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by more than a factor of 2 for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism that continuously remodels the local electrostatic landscape, providing an additional molecular-scale pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerating ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that dynamic nanoscale charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ion-conducting hydrogels and suggest alternative strategies for nanostructured membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.

item.title: Nano Letters: Long-Range Single-Molecule Transport and Assembly at Liquid Nitrogen Temperatures
item.description:
Tairan Yang, Zhiwen Zhu, Cunzhe Lou, Juan Xiang, Qi Huang, Yizhang Li, Jie Li, Qiang Sun
The bottom-up construction of functional matter from individually positioned atoms and molecules requires deterministic control over capture, transport, and assembly on surfaces. Although atomic manipulation is well established, extending comparable control to molecules remains challenging due to their complex internal degrees of freedom and surface interactions. Here, we demonstrate controlled single-molecule transport and assembly at liquid nitrogen temperatures using a scanning tunneling microscope. We designed a molecule with an intrinsic electric dipole moment, enabling efficient noncontact manipulation via electrostatic coupling to the tip. This strategy allows stable long-range translation and the programmable formation of defined dimers and larger assemblies. Systematic mapping of the operational parameter space, supported by first-principles calculations, identifies an electrostatic driving mechanism governing motion. Our approach shifts molecular nanomachine research from demonstrations under extreme cryogenic conditions to positional control under experimentally more accessible temperatures, establishing a practical platform for programmable molecular-scale engineering.

item.title: Nano Letters: Stacking-Order-Dependent Electronic Properties of MoTe2/WSe2 Moiré Bilayers
item.description:
Zhongdong Han, Wenjin Zhao, Eegene Clara Chung, Chia-Hao Lee, Zui Tao, Zhengchao Xia, Yichi Zhang, Yiyu Xia, et al.
Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré bilayers have realized a wide range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena. The physics in these materials is often sensitive to the interlayer stacking order. Polarization-resolved optical second harmonic generation (SHG) is the most used technique for stacking order characterization but unverified for most heterobilayers. Here we calibrate the optical SHG for angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers by the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). We directly compare the transport and magnetic properties and the electronic phase diagram for two distinct stacking orders. With the calibrated stacking order assignment, we clarify the interpretation of earlier results, including the nature of the Chern insulator, mechanism of an electric-field-tuned metal–insulator transition at half band filling, and the Kondo lattice physics. Our work provides a consistent picture of the relation between the stacking order and the electronic properties of MoTe2/WSe2 moiré bilayers.

item.title: Nano Letters: Giant Resistance Switching Ratio Exceeding 106 through a Reversible 2D–3D Structural Phase Transition in Nonequilibrium (Pb1– x Sn x )Se Thin Films
item.description:
Naoto Hoshi, Sota Abe, Sangjin Choi, Kota Hanzawa, Hiroto Arima, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Shogo Hatayama, Hidenori Hiramatsu, et al.
Control and switching of electrical resistance in semiconductors are important for high-performance electronic devices. Here, we realize giant resistance switching in nonequilibrium (Pb1–xSnx)Se films through a reversible structural transition between three-dimensional (3D) rock-salt (RS)-type and two-dimensional (2D) GeS-type phases. The solid-solution films were fabricated by reactive solid-phase epitaxy of SnSe/PbSe bilayers followed by rapid thermal quenching. Se-flux annealing of the PbSe template suppressed Pb precipitation, enabling chemically homogeneous, single-phase nonequilibrium RS-type films up to x = 0.58. Increasing the Sn content from x = 0.43 to 0.58 systematically increased the 2D–3D structural transition temperature and enhanced the resistance switching ratio to 4.9 × 106, far exceeding those of representative transition-metal oxide thin films (∼102–104). The giant resistance switching originates from the nearly complete transformation (∼98%) of the conductive 3D phase into the high-resistance 2D phase. These results establish crystal-dimensionality switching as a promising new mechanism for high-performance electronic switching devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Chirality-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enantioselective Neuroprotection with Restored Neuroactive Signaling in Alzheimer’s Disease
item.description:
Lulu He, Zhen He, Zhangcong Yu, Hongying Bao, Qishu Zhang, Xiaolin Duan, Aiguo Wu, Juan Li
Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and a cascade of interconnected neurotoxic events, including oxidative stress, glutamate excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, and impaired neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling. To address the multifactorial nature of AD pathology, chiral d- or l-cysteine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles are developed as a multitarget nanotherapeutic platform. Both enantiomers effectively inhibit Aβ aggregation, scavenge reactive oxygen species, reduce extracellular glutamate levels, and attenuate calcium dysregulation. In parallel, d/l-Cys-COFs rescue compromised neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling, as evidenced by normalized expression of neuropeptide Y and brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In transgenic AD mice, d/l-Cys-COF treatment significantly improves memory and cognitive performance. Notably, the d-enantiomer affords superior neuroprotection through enhanced suppression of pathological intracellular calcium overload, whereas restoration of neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling remains chirality-independent. These findings identify chirality as a key design element for multitarget nanotherapeutics against AD, with enantioselective efficacy arising primarily from differential regulation of calcium dysregulation and shared restoration of neuroactive signaling contributing to the overall therapeutic benefit.

item.title: JACS: Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy Reveals Hidden Coherence in Molecular Aggregates
item.description:
Mingran Zhang, Yihe Xu, Vladislav V. Yakovlev, Zhedong Zhang
Ultrafast spectroscopy of complex molecules has been achieved under light–matter coupling by the use of laser pulses and single photons. Yet, the excited-state dynamics essential to photochemistry is suffering from the convolution of multiple relaxation pathways and limited resolution in nonlinear signal, which still remain challenging. To address these, we develop time-resolved quantum ghost spectroscopy (tr-QGS) with entangled light, which enables a background-free detection of excited-state emission while offering precise control over temporal resolution. We apply this approach to perylene bisimide (PBI-1) trimers by combining a quantum description of light-molecule interaction with time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (TD-DMRG) simulations. This explicitly includes five vibrational modes and nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states. Our simulations reveal that tr-QGS captures electronic coherence oscillating at 0.6 eV for ∼50 fs, a signature of nonadiabatic coupling that was obscured in time-resolved measurements. Moreover, we observe a direct transfer from electronic to vibrational coherence at 200 fs, providing real-time visualization of vibronic relaxation pathways. Photon entanglement eliminates background noise and ground-state bleaching artifacts, which plague time-resolved measurements. These results establish tr-QGS as a transformative tool for interrogating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular aggregates, light-harvesting complexes, and photocatalysts, offering a route to reveal quantum coherence effects in chemistry with unprecedented precision.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ultrasensitive Enantioselective Chiroptical Sensing with Large-Area Twisted Aligned Carbon Nanotube Films
item.description:
Haoyu Xie, Jichao Fan, Zarif Ahmad Razin Bhuiyan, Saqlain Raza, Mohammad Mohammadi, Cheng Guo, Yunshan Wang, Jun Liu, et al.
Enantioselective chiroptical sensing is gaining traction across various applications. However, intrinsic molecular chiroptical responses are weak, and existing amplification approaches add synthesis, manufacturing, or operational complexity that limits sensitivity and scalability. Here, we present an enantioselective sensing paradigm merging adsorption-driven chirality induction with large-scale optical transduction in twisted stacks of aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) films. Chiral molecules adsorb onto CNTs to form chiroptically active composites that are macroscopically assembled by alignment and rotational stacking, yielding large ultraviolet circular dichroism (CD). We resolve enantiomer handedness and quantify concentration in single-enantiomer aqueous solutions using a single sensor without lithography, hotspot delivery, or a paired opposite-handed reference. We achieve high sensitivity with estimated sub-μM minimum detectable concentrations for glucose and provide a proof-of-concept demonstration with alanine. Neither analyte-only solution shows detectable CD under the present measurement conditions. We demonstrate Langmuir-type adsorption behavior using molecular dynamics simulations and reproduce experimental results using optical simulations. This platform provides a foundation for future development toward cost-effective in situ enantiomer monitoring in aqueous environments.

item.title: JACS: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
item.description:
Mouma Chatterjee, Vinay Ambekar Ranganath, Shashikumar Haranal, Mukesh Kumar, Suman Kalyan Sahoo, Indrajit Maity
Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

item.title: Nano Letters: Programming-Current-Induced Mechanism Crossover Enables Reconfigurable Memory Window in In2Te3 Selector-Only Memory
item.description:
Mengfei Zhang, Yuting Sun, Xi Li, Zhitang Song, Min Zhu
Selector-only memory (SOM), which integrates threshold switching and data storage within a chalcogenide layer, is a promising high-density memory technology, yet the regulation of memory characteristics and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that programming current (Ip) regulates the competition between composition-driven and trap-associated switching processes in amorphous In2Te3 devices. Decreasing Ip from 10–2 to 10–4 A reversibly changes the positive-read threshold voltage (Vth) ordering from Vth, SET > Vth, RESET, yielding an inverted memory window of up to 1.53 V, to Vth, SET < Vth, RESET, with a conventional memory window of ∼0.5 V. Cross-sectional energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals state-dependent In/Te redistribution at high Ip, consistent with composition-mediated modulation of conductive pathways. At low Ip, atomic redistribution is suppressed and trap-associated transport modulation is enhanced, with extracted trap depths of 0.51 eV (SET) and 0.63 eV (RESET), establishing Ip as a means of modifying SOM memory characteristics without complex engineering.

item.title: ACS Nano: Strain-Engineered Deterministic Quantum Dots for Telecom O-Band Emission Using Buried Stressors
item.description:
Imad Limame, Ching-Wen Shih, Kartik Gaur, Martin Podhorský, Sarthak Tripathi, Setthanat Wijitpatima, Dominik M. Feder, Maximilian Ries, et al.
The deterministic realization of quantum light sources operating at telecom wavelengths is essential for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate that telecom O-band emission can be achieved from site-controlled InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots (QDs). Our concept utilizes a buried AlAs/AlOx stressor layer with the unique feature of inducing a well-defined and controllable tensile strain field at the growth surface, enabling both site-selective nucleation at the mesa’s centers and a redshift of QD emission to the ∼1.3 μm wavelength range. This concept not only eliminates the need for strain-reducing layers (SRLs), which are known to degrade optical coherence, but also provides spatial control and spectral tunability. The grown telecom QDs show single-photon emission with g(2)(0) = (5.0 ± 1.0) × 10–2 at 4 K and (2.8 ± 0.3) × 10–1 at 77 K, demonstrating the quantum nature and thermal stability of the emitters. The emission characteristics of complex excitonic states are analyzed using 8-band k·p and configuration-interaction modeling, which quantitatively reproduces the experimental observations. Finally, we present a theory-supported strategy to further redshift the emission toward the center of the O-band and beyond by employing a multiburied stressor approach. This combined framework of experiment and theory establishes the buried stressor concept as a scalable route toward highly coherent, position-controlled O-band quantum emitters compatible with scalable photonic integration.

item.title: Nano Letters: Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
item.description:
Zhongyu Liu, Zhenghao Xu, Li Zheng, Xuetong Zhou, Lingyan Shen, Xinhong Cheng, Zhijun Ning
Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

item.title: Nano Letters: Spontaneous Nanoscale Wiggling in Cleaved WTe2
item.description:
Si-Hong Lee, Minsuk Suh, Seong Ho Lim, Youngjae Kim, Jungpil Seo
Structural deformation of crystal lattices has emerged as a powerful pathway to engineer and boost electronic properties through lattice geometry. However, realizing ultrafine structural modulations remains challenging without external strain imposed by substrates, prestrain, or artificial patterning. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy, we show that the cleaving process spontaneously induces nanoscale wiggling in 1T′-WTe2 without such external strain sources. Furthermore, scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals pronounced electronic reconstruction and spatially resolved spectral modulations between the top and valley regions of the wiggling. Combined with first-principles calculations, our results show that this wiggling substantially modifies the local electronic structure relative to the unstrained flat region, suggesting electronic structure reconstruction driven by spontaneous lattice deformation. These findings establish spontaneous nanoscale wiggling as a self-formed structural modulation for local electronic-structure engineering in strain-sensitive low-symmetry layered materials.

item.title: JACS: Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
item.description:
Zhongtang Yu, Hailong Zhao, Caiping Tian, Xiuwen Yu, You-liang Zeng, Yu Liu, Jiaxuan Chen, Qiong Wu, et al.
Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

item.title: JACS: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
item.description:
Andreas Ghosh, Kai Cui, D. Vale Cofer-Shabica, Joseph E. Subotnik, Sharon Hammes-Schiffer
Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

item.title: ACS Nano: Au Nanoparticle-Functionalized Antheraea pernyi Silk Nanofibrils: A Spatially Adaptive Anti-Inflammatory and Pro-Regenerative Paradigm for Disparate Chronic Epithelial Diseases
item.description:
Peng Zhou, Fuying Liao, Zenghao Chen, Ga Liu, Shengfei Bao, Yingui Cao, Zhen Zhu, Xiao Yang, et al.
Management of disparate chronic epithelial diseases relies on fragmented site-specific protocols yet remains hindered by common pathological barriers and sustained inflammation. Herein, we developed a top-down strategy to exfoliate short nanofibrils from Antheraea pernyi silk fibers featuring inherent Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) motifs, followed by in situ growth of Au nanoparticles. The resulting platform (Au@ASFs) achieved superior spatial adaptability via catalytic oxygen propulsion, navigating across barriers to reach deep-seated lesions. Once localized, Au@ASFs provided phase-spanning multifunctional therapy through near-infrared (NIR)-triggered photothermal sterilization. Through RGD–integrin interactions, they also promoted hemostasis and M2 macrophage polarization to resolve persistent inflammation while enhancing fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and neuronal differentiation. In vivo, Au@ASFs (+NIR) significantly improved closure of infected diabetic oral ulcers from 43.1 to 95.5% by day 7 and restored colon length in ulcerative colitis from 66.3 to 97.7% of healthy controls. In infected diabetic wounds, Au@ASFs (+NIR) increased closure from 63.8 to 89.1% by day 14. Transcriptomic analysis of wound tissues revealed reprogramming through suppressed NF-κB inflammatory signaling, activated Wnt5a/GSK-3β signaling for neuronal differentiation, and modulated PI3K-Akt signaling for tissue regeneration. Collectively, Au@ASF (+NIR) consistently resolves chronic epithelial diseases across disparate anatomical sites, establishing a unified drug-free paradigm that transcends site-specific constraints.

item.title: JACS: Amorphous Halide Cathodes Enable 75C All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
item.description:
Yuhao Duan, Feng Wan, Fiaz Hussain, Jiuwei Lei, Zihan Song, Paul R. Shearing, Wei Xia, Zhuangjun Fan, et al.
Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity. Despite lower bulk Li+ conductivity, amorphous LiVCl4 dramatically reduces GB-associated interfacial resistance and enables a catholyte-free cathode (CAM content: 90 wt %) to deliver a capacity of 74.3 mAh g–1 at 5 mA cm–2, compared with 10.2 mAh g–1 for the crystalline counterpart. Meanwhile, the ASSLB further operates across a wide temperature range from −30 to 60 °C and achieves 84.2% capacity utilization at an ultrahigh A-LiVCl4 areal loading of 53.4 mg cm–2. Coupled with amorphous LiTaOCl4, the ASSLB achieves 102.1 mAh g–1 at 20 mA cm–2 (∼75C) and retains 82.3% capacity after 16,000 cycles. These results establish amorphization-enabled conformal interfaces as a new paradigm for ultrahigh-power ASSLBs.

item.title: JACS: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
item.description:
Chenyang Gao, Tingting Xia, Shengyu Zhang, Xianqing Wu, Wei-Hong Zhu, Jingping Qu, Yifeng Chen
Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

item.title: ACS Nano: Emergent Higher-Order Optical Nonlinearity in Self-Assembled Polar Supertextures
item.description:
Daniel A. Bustamante Lopez, Deepankar Sri Gyan, Xiaojiang Li, Vladimir A. Stoica, Sujit Das, Peter Meisenheimer, Akash Surampalli, Mohit Tanwani, et al.
Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

item.title: JACS: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
item.description:
Fan Zhou, Qing Hao, Youxian Li, Panke Zhou, Bingbing Gao, Qiongfeng Shi, Dong Wang, Hong Liu
Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

item.title: JACS: Macrocycle Size-Controlled Dynamic and Static Chirality in Donor–Acceptor [2]Catenanes
item.description:
Kai Lan, Rong Luo, Jin Yin, Jiao Ming, Dongmei Zhang, Qianqian Wang, Yan Hu, Jiaming Huang, et al.
Chiral [2]catenanes, a prominent class of mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), can exhibit either static or dynamic mechanostereochemistry. Controlling these mechanostereochemical states without altering the covalent connectivity, however, remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of chiral [2]catenanes derived from ExBox and cycloparaphenyleneperylene (CPPP), whose dynamic behavior is altered by the size of the CPPP macrocycle. We identified a sharp, size-dependent threshold: The conformational stereogenic unit of [7]CPPP is kinetically locked, whereas those of [8]CPPP and [9]CPPP are dynamic at room temperature. This conformational stereochemistry strongly biases the co-conformational stereochemistry in the catenane, effectively resulting in a single dominant diastereomer. This effective coupling of the two stereogenic units allows the conformational stereochemistry to be biased by the ion pairing of the interlocked cationic ring with a chiral anion. This research highlights the potential of mechanically interlocked architectures for controlling the dynamic mechanostereochemistry.

item.title: JACS: Harnessing Surface Wrinkling Instability for Visualizing Dynamic Chemistry in Polymer Networks
item.description:
Mengling Yang, Shuzhen Yan, Yuchan Liao, Wenbin Wang, Xueliang Jiang, Xuesong Jiang, Xuzhou Yan
Studying dynamic chemical behaviors is fundamental to understanding and regulating the dynamic responses and functions of polymer materials. However, real-time, intuitive, and selective visualization of these molecular processes─particularly when multiple dynamic motifs coexist─remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce surface wrinkles as a visualization platform that directly translates dynamic chemical behaviors in polymers into observable macroscopic morphological changes. Using a dual-cross-linked polymer network (DCN) containing quadruple hydrogen bonds and mechanical bonds as a model system, we fabricate stable wrinkles via modulus mismatch in a bilayer architecture. In situ microscopy reveals that acid-triggered dissociation of quadruple hydrogen bonds causes rapid wrinkle erasure due to network disruption, whereas base-induced rotaxane sliding leads to gradual wrinkle erasure owing to network relaxation, reflecting their distinct dynamic mechanisms and time scales. Rheological analyses on single-cross-linked model networks corroborate these macroscopic observations at the molecular level. Moreover, by programming wrinkle patterns with “write–hide–read” functionality, we achieve macroscopic visualization and differentiation of microscopic dynamic processes. This work establishes surface wrinkling as a powerful and intuitive platform for real-time monitoring of dynamic chemistry and provides valuable insights for designing functional polymer materials with tunable macroscopic properties.

item.title: ACS Nano: Synergistic Tuning of Diffusion Enables Surface-Passivation-Directed Electrodeposition of Shaped Bimetallic Nanoparticles
item.description:
Gabriel C. Halford, Abigail M. Sublett, Adam J. Buratowski, Kaelyn M. Harmon, Harikrishnan N. Nambiar, Michelle L. Personick
Many applications for shape-controlled metal nanoparticles require their immobilization on a surface, creating a need for development of direct substrate-based synthesis routes for increasingly complex materials. Colloidal chemical syntheses for shape-controlled nanoparticles are common, but transferring insight from synthesis in solution to growth on a substrate requires accounting for significant differences in reagent diffusion between these two growth environments─a nontrivial challenge. In the present work, we establish fundamental principles for rationally adapting reaction parameters from colloidal syntheses to electrodeposition such that the growth of nanoparticles on the electrode proceeds under comparable reagent diffusion conditions to those that drive shape direction during colloidal growth. To demonstrate these principles, we successfully translate reaction conditions from colloidal synthesis to electrodeposition for a series of dilute bimetallic (silver) gold nanoparticles whose shapes are controlled by surface deposition of silver: concave cubes, octahedra, rhombic dodecahedra, truncated ditetragonal prisms, and tetrahexahedra. By comparing open-circuit potential measurements of the colloidal syntheses with chronopotentiometry measurements from galvanostatic electrodeposition, we determine the adjustments required to establish ideal growth kinetics for each electrodeposition. We identify specific synthetic handles─mode of mass transport, surfactant concentration, applied current density, and secondary metal concentration─required to modulate reagent transport to the electrode surface, as well as the direction they must be modified so that the relative rates of silver and gold ion reduction mimic colloidal growth. These generalizable synthetic parameters for controlling reagent diffusion and concentrations near the electrode surface open possibilities for the electrodeposition of complex multimetallic and shaped nanomaterials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Phase Homogenization via Decoupled Nucleation and Growth for High-Efficiency Quasi-Two-Dimensional Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
item.description:
Peijin Ma, Shujie Huang, Yizhao Qing, Bing Han, Changxiao Li, Biao Zhao, Zhan’ao Tan
Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites with multiquantum-well structures hold great potential for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) due to their cascaded energy funnels, yet their performance is hampered by defect-rich low-n phases and disordered crystallization. Here, we present a phase-homogenization strategy that combines a self-adaptive solvent by doping ethyl acetate (EA) with dimethyl phosphonate (DPP), which simultaneously modulates the polarity and evaporation kinetics of EA, guiding the crystal growth and phase distribution of quasi-2D perovskites. The strong coordination of DPP with Pb2+ also passivates deep-level traps, thereby drastically reducing nonradiative low-n-phase recombination. We further use the bridging molecules to enhance perovskite/transport layer interfaces by incorporating sodium 4-amino-1-naphthalenesulfonate tetrahydrate (SANT) into the PEDOT/PSS hole transport layer, which weakens PEDOT–PSS electrostatic attraction, enhancing conductivity while reducing acid-induced corrosion of the ITO electrode and perovskite film. SANT also templates perovskite nucleation via its functional groups, promoting ordered crystallite growth. Overall, the resulting green-emitting quasi-2D perovskite LEDs achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.81% (average 30.74%) and a luminance of 44338 cd m–2, with a lower surface temperature during operation. Moreover, the devices exhibit a 10-fold enhancement in operational stability compared to the control counterparts. Our findings provide a strategy for combining crystallization control and interface passivation in quasi-2D PeLEDs.

item.title: JACS: Bridging Spectroscopy and Reactivity: Identifying the True Reactive CO Species in Electrocatalytic CO Oxidation
item.description:
Tian-Yi Yang, Ya-Jun Huang, Hao-Fei Geng, Hai-Sheng Su, Jing-Xin Huang, Can Shao, Jin-Rui Liao, Guo-Kun Liu, et al.
In situ electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy has revolutionized our understanding of electrocatalysis. However, establishing a rigorous correlation between spectroscopic signatures and reaction kinetics is still very challenging because high-coverage surface species may dominate the signal, whereas the truly reactive participants may be short-lived or spectroscopically silent. To disentangle spectators from true reaction participants, we developed a high-sensitivity spectroelectrochemical platform that integrates the rotating disk electrode with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (RDE-SERS). This approach enables the simultaneous acquisition of reaction kinetics and interfacial molecular information under well-defined mass transport conditions. Using this versatile approach, we investigated the benchmark carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) on the Pt surface, which enabled decoupling between the spectroscopically observable species and the catalytically active species. Despite persistent and intense Raman signatures of adsorbed CO (COad) in the diffusion-limited region, COad predominantly acts as a spectator that blocks surface sites without effectively participating in the reaction, as confirmed by the isotope substitution experiments. Conversely, the oxidation current is sustained by the continuous flux of solution-phase CO (COsol), which is identified as the kinetically relevant reactant. These findings offer a new perspective on the roles of adsorbed species versus solution-phase species during dynamic electrochemical reactions. Collectively, the RDE-SERS methodology is established as a reliable strategy for identifying true reaction pathways, bridging molecular-level spectroscopic identification with macroscopic reactivity in complex electrocatalytic systems.

item.title: JACS: Highly Selective Artificial Lithium Channels
item.description:
Harekrushna Behera, Tyler J. Duncan, Laxmicharan Samineni, Hyeonji Oh, Chenhao Yao, Raman Dhiman, Siqi Wang, Luke Hatch, et al.
Sustainable mining and recycling of lithium (Li) have the potential to offer a secure and reliable global supply of lithium to meet rapidly growing energy-storage demands. Bioinspired technologies have the potential to increase sustainability and reduce the environmental impacts of lithium purification. In this study, we report the design of a class of bioinspired supramolecular membrane channels that, to the best of our knowledge, achieve one of the highest overall Li+ selectivities reported to date for artificial transmembrane ion channels, with conservative lower-limit selectivity estimates of Li+/Na+ ≥ 94, Li+/K+ ≥ 136, Li+/Mg2+ ≥ 286, and Li+/Ca2+ ≥ 228 under electrochemically driven transport conditions, thereby establishing a new benchmark for Li+-selective membrane channels. The single-channel conductance of this channel for Li+ ions was determined to be 13.35 pS, equating to Li+ ion transport rates of approximately 1.34 × 107 ions/s per channel at −160 mV. These channels were constructed using a central-ring pillar[5]arene appended with alkyl chains ending in diphenylphosphine oxide (DPP) ligands. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that Li+ selectivity arises from coupled hydration-shell retention, ion-ligand coordination at the DPP-functionalized entrance, and confinement effects within the LAP5n10-DPP channel. At the DPP-functionalized entrance, Li+ retains much of its compact hydration shell while engaging the phosphoryl oxygen through a favorable ligand-exchange interaction, whereas Na+ interacts with the DPP region primarily through a water-separated outer-shell geometry, and K+ interacts more strongly with the adjacent hydrophobic/phenyl-rich region. At the central constriction, all ions experience hydration-shell disruption, but divalent Ca2+ and Mg2+ face the largest dehydration penalties because pore passage would require near-complete dehydration of their strongly bound hydration shells.

item.title: ACS Nano: Mechanics-Guided Conformal Probes Enable Crystallographically Resolved Anisotropic Interlayer Friction Measurements in Low-Symmetry 2D Materials
item.description:
Tianyan Gao, Shuping Shang, Zeyan Xie, Jiahao Li, Xinshuai Peng, Xin’an Chen, Xuebo Yuan, Guorui Wang, et al.
Interlayer sliding in two-dimensional (2D) materials is generally assumed to be weakly anisotropic, even as low-symmetry layered crystals with strongly direction-dependent properties continue to emerge. Here we adopt a mechanics-guided conformal probe design that enables quantitative measurement of crystallographically resolved interlayer friction between anisotropic 2D materials. Using Ta2NiSe5 as a model system, we demonstrate pronounced interlayer friction anisotropy approaching 2 orders of magnitude, substantially larger than its moderate in-plane friction anisotropy and the values reported for high-symmetry layered materials. Atomic-resolution lateral force mapping reveals a hierarchical friction landscape composed of atomic lattice corrugation and twist-induced moiré modulation, with the moiré wavelength evolving systematically with relative misorientation. These results show that interlayer friction in low-symmetry 2D materials is governed by a multiscale, orientation-dependent potential energy landscape and constitutes an independent mechanical degree of freedom. The conformal probe platform provides a general route to probe and engineer direction-selective interlayer mechanics in van der Waals systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Threefold-Symmetric Te Nanoparticles for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes
item.description:
Jiawei Su, ChangChun Fan, Zhuoyuan Li, Weiguang Lan, Guoming Lin, Wenhui Wang, Mingjie Liu
Uncontrolled Zn nucleation and growth at the electrode–electrolyte interface limit the reversibility and lifetime of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Nanoparticle (NP)-based anode protective layers are widely used to regulate Zn deposition, yet precise control over the exposed zincophilic facets of individual NPs remains challenging. Here, we show a facet-geometry engineering strategy based on threefold-symmetric Te nanoparticles (TF–Te NPs) to modulate Zn plating/stripping during cycling. The TF–Te NPs present a high density of zincophilic facets, while their threefold symmetric geometry spatially clusters nucleation sites within nanoscale proximity, promoting uniform Zn deposition and accelerating interfacial kinetics. As a result, TF–Te NP-modified Zn anodes exhibit reduced nucleation overpotentials, improved rate capability, and enhanced cycling stability. Our work establishes a direct link between NP geometry, facet-dependent zincophilicity, and Zn deposition behavior, offering a strategy for engineering NP protective layers across a broad range of aqueous batteries.

item.title: JACS: Smallest Endohedral Water Cage Featuring a Nonclassic Polyhedron: Experimental Observation of (H2O)17
item.description:
Wenhui Yan, Yang-Yang Zhang, Shuai Jiang, Shangdong Li, Tiantong Wang, Jun-Bo Lu, Han-Shi Hu, Jiayue Yang, et al.
The structural transition from clustered water molecules to the hydrogen-bonding networks of bulk liquid defines one of the most fundamental problems in physical chemistry, yet the precise size at which the endohedral cages emerge remains experimentally elusive. While theory has long predicted that a fully encapsulated water molecule requires a minimum of 16–23 surrounding molecules, direct experimental identification has been hindered by the difficulty of size selection of neutral clusters. Using infrared spectroscopy coupled to vacuum-ultraviolet threshold photoionization, we provide the first experimental evidence that (H2O)17 forms the smallest water endohedral cage, achieving a decades-standing goal of establishing the molecular limit of a solvation shell. Surprisingly, the oxygen framework of this (H2O)17 cage defines an unprecedented, nonclassic polyhedron with four tetragonal, four pentagonal, and two hexagonal faces that breaks the symmetry constraints of all classical Platonic, Archimedean, and Johnson solids. This work establishes a critical structural precursor to the hydrogen-bonding network topology observed in condensed-phase water and offers new perspectives at the multidisciplinary sciences of mathematics, materials, physics, and chemistry.

item.title: ACS Nano: Subshell-Confined Symmetry Lowering and Prolonged Excited-State Dynamics in Large Silver Nanoclusters
item.description:
Li Tang, Weinan Dong, Xiaofei Wang, Xue Bai, Shuo Zhang, Zhennan Wu, Shuxin Wang
Symmetry breaking has the potential to counteract the shortening of excited-state lifetimes with increasing nuclearity and metallicity but is difficult to accomplish in large nanoclusters, whose multishell frameworks are strongly coupled. Here, we report a four-shell silver nanocluster, Ag104, in which the principal reconstruction is concentrated in an Ag52S22 subsurface shell, and whose inner core and outer ligand-protected motifs retain closely similar topologies relative to its highly symmetric Ag100 analogue – a structurally related pair that enables the correlations accompanying localized symmetry distortion to be examined. The two clusters also differ in composition and thiolate substitution pattern, so the comparison probes coupled structural and electronic changes. Electronic-structure calculations and real-space charge analyses showed that subshell-confined symmetry breaking lifts electronic degeneracies, redistributes oscillator strength, and induces pronounced spatial charge separation, thereby reducing electron–hole overlap. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy further revealed an unexpected order-of-magnitude increase in carrier lifetime from ∼500 ps in Ag100 to ∼5 ns in Ag104 and distinctly activated phonon-assisted relaxation in Ag100 compared to Ag104. This establishes a strategy for engineering large atomically precise nanoclusters with long-lived excited states.

item.title: ACS Nano: Watching Electrochemical Interfaces in Motion with High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy
item.description:
Ehsan Rahimi
Electrochemical processes involve transient phenomena, including nucleation and growth, phase transformations, dissolution, ion transport, and interfacial restructuring, which are difficult to capture simultaneously at nanoscale and in real time under electrochemical controls. High-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), originally developed for dynamic biological imaging, combines nanometer-scale spatial resolution with frame times of approximately 0.1–5 s/frame, extending into the subsecond regime, enabling direct visualization of electrochemical interfaces under operando conditions. This perspective highlights emerging applications of HS-AFM in electrochemistry, including electrodeposition, nanoparticle dissolution, corrosion, lithiation-induced morphological evolution, protein adsorption, and nanobubble dynamics. HS-AFM reveals that mechanistic insight often resides in transient, nonequilibrium pathways rather than equilibrium structures alone. Advances will enable real-time nanoscale correlation of interfacial structure, kinetics, and electrochemical function.

item.title: ACS Nano: Disulfidptosis-Driven Immune-Activated Multimodal Therapy for Glioblastoma with Systemic Safety Control
item.description:
Meng Zhang, Chenteng Lin, Khishigjargal Ganbat, Wei Meng, Heemin Kang, Wenjia Gao, Hongyuan Li, Guangwei Jiang, et al.
Effective glioblastoma therapy requires simultaneous solutions to poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration, insufficient tumor-selective killing, and treatment-related systemic toxicity. We hypothesized that a BBB-penetrating nanoplatform capable of generating distinct H2S exposures in tumor and normal tissues could enhance antitumor efficacy while mitigating doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity. Here, DOX-loaded metastable molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers functionalized with an I6P8 peptide (DOX@MSI) were developed. After BBB transport and tumor accumulation, the acidic, H2O2-rich, and GSH-rich microenvironment accelerates nanoplatform degradation, promoting GSH depletion and enhanced H2S/DOX release. High local H2S upregulates xCT, while H2S/DOX-mediated mitochondrial inhibition suppresses NADPH regeneration, synergistically triggering disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, H2S suppresses the JAK2/STAT3/IDO axis, alleviating DOX-induced immunosuppression and enhancing immunogenic cell death and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In contrast, slower degradation under physiological conditions enables sustained low-level H2S release, reducing the level of oxidative stress and ERK-associated apoptosis in cardiomyocytes. Together with NIR-enhanced photothermal therapy, DOX@MSI suppresses orthotopic glioblastoma while reducing cardiac injury, thereby integrating tumor-selective multimodal therapy with active organ protection.

item.title: ACS Nano: All-in-One Mitochondria-Targeted Iron-Based MOF “Nanomissiles” for Synergistically Potentiated Tumor Ferroptosis, Dual Phototherapy, and Chemotherapy
item.description:
Hang Li, Xuezhong Du
Pronounced heterogeneity and adaptability of tumors inherently curtail monotherapeutic efficacy, necessitating rationally integrated multimodal regimens that enable precise intervention, overcome resistance, and eradicate heterogeneous cell populations within the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). All-in-one mitochondria-targeted “nanomissiles” were created by emodin (Em)-Fe3+-gated, doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded PCN-600(FeIII) (denoted as DOX@ME) nanoparticles for synergistic multimodal tumor therapy integrating ferroptosis, photodynamic therapy (PDT), mild photothermal therapy (MPTT), and chemotherapy. DOX@ME achieved on-demand release of DOX in response to the TME [such as low pH, glutathione (GSH), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP)] and near-infrared laser, via the disassembly of the Em-Fe3+ gating films and/or the degradation of the PCN-600(FeIII) nanocarriers. Under both 660 and 808 nm laser irradiation, DOX@ME effectively triggered apoptosis via chemotherapy, PDT, and MPTT while robustly accelerating reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, GSH depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation, and lipid peroxide (LPO) accumulation to enhance ferroptosis. Moreover, DOX@ME could alleviate thermotolerance by depleting intracellular ATP and downregulating protective heat shock protein 70 to boost the curative efficacy of MPTT. DOX@ME exhibited excellent antitumor efficacy and good biocompatibility and biosafety in A549 tumor-bearing nude mice. Collectively, DOX@ME demonstrates robust clinical translational potential for precision cancer therapy.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanoscale Immune Activator for Enhancing CD8+ T Cell Infiltration in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
item.description:
Deyu Zhang, Dongxin Peng, Xin Wang, Yuting Gao, Zhuang Liu, Rui Yang, Ting Wei, Chengkun Li, et al.
The infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment is a well-established determinant of immunotherapy efficacy and patient prognosis. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing this process and the therapeutic strategies capable of modulating it remain largely unexplored. Here, we identify HCC-IN-247 as a candidate compound that enhances IFNβ-driven CD8+ T cell infiltration both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the long noncoding RNA LINC02084 directly interacts with the transcription factor GLIS1 and facilitates its recruitment to the IFNβ promoter. HCC-IN-247 was identified through screening to target the LINC02084-GLIS1 binding interface, thereby stabilizing this RNA–protein complex. Stabilization of the complex significantly enhances IFNβ transcription, which in turn upregulates CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression and promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration. Furthermore, this study engineered a nanoparticle-based delivery system, designated Lip@RA@BSA-PD-L1/IN-247, for the codelivery of HCC-IN-247 and the anti-PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in HCC treatment. These nanoparticles exhibited robust tumor-specific accumulation and elicited potent synergistic antitumor activity against HCC in mice. Collectively, our findings establish HCC-IN-247 as an activator of the tumor immune microenvironment and provide a preclinical basis for a combined immunotherapeutic approach to HCC.

item.title: JACS: Highly Enantioselective Synthesis of 1,2,3-Trisubstituted Cyclopropanes through DNA-Catalyzed Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky Cyclopropanation
item.description:
Yang Zheng, Rao Dai, Yun-Lin Li, Sze Ian Joel Loke, Cheng-Qian Song, Qi Shi, Lin-Wei Wang, Ru-Yi Zhu
Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.

item.title: JACS: Vacancy-Induced Ligand-Hole Character Redirects Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
item.description:
Jihun Jeong, Dayeon Choi, Lulu Lyu, Seongkoo Kang, Gi-Hyeok Lee, Hyungjun Kim, Wanli Yang, Yong-Mook Kang
Li-rich layered oxides access high capacities through the combined participation of transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen oxidation is often coupled with irreversible structural rearrangement and voltage decay. Here, we show that oxygen-vacancy-preconditioning modifies the local Ni–O electronic structure and promotes oxygen-derived ligand-hole character in a Li-rich layered oxide. High-temperature quasi-single-crystal (QSC) formation generates oxygen-deficient local environments while preserving the overall layered framework. Synchrotron spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveals enhanced Ni–O hybridization and redistribution of charge compensation toward oxygen-derived states. Mapping resonant inelastic X-ray scattering further shows earlier oxygen participation during charging, followed by increased delocalization of oxygen-derived holes within hybridized transition-metal–oxygen states. This modified redox pathway suppresses Mn reduction and is coupled to a distinct structural response in which transient lattice environments formed during the initial cycle progressively relax during prolonged cycling, while the layered framework is largely retained. The resulting cathode exhibits reduced voltage hysteresis and voltage decay, together with improved electrochemical reversibility. These results establish a direct connection between vacancy-modified ligand-hole character and oxygen-redox-driven structural relaxation, demonstrating how local electronic structure governs the structural pathway of oxygen-redox-active layered oxides.

item.title: JACS: Understanding the Instability Origin for Design of Robust Pure RuO2 Anode Catalyst in PEM Water Electrolysis
item.description:
Lin-Lin Wang, Xuan-Xuan Cheng, Xiao-Long Zhang, Xiao-Ran Wang, Cuo Wu, Jing-Jing Li, Xue-Rong Qin, Hang Yin, et al.
Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.

item.title: JACS: Noncovalent Metal–Water Polarization Governs Helmholtz Capacitance
item.description:
Lang Li, Elias Diesen, Nicolas G. Hörmann, Karsten Reuter
Electrified metal–water interfaces govern charge storage and electrochemical reactivity, yet the microscopic origin of their metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance has remained unresolved. Here, we use extensive density functional theory-based ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to reproduce and explain the long-established experimental capacitance trend at fcc(111) metal–water interfaces. We show that this trend is governed primarily by the electrode-side electronic response of the explicit metal–water interface, which controls the effective electron spillover length and, hence, the bias capacitance.
